Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a well-circumscribed, round pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe. In the context of the provided options, this appearance is most consistent with a hematogenous metastasis from a known extrathoracic malignancy like colonic leiomyosarcoma, which typically presents as discrete, rounded nodules ("cannonball" lesions) rather than the spiculated mass of primary lung cancer or the calcified/popcorn appearance of a hamartoma.
